dedupe_keys.name: gao 21 297 fcc role in restoring telecommunications after hurricane maria

description: This report of the US Government Accountability Office, Telecommunications: FCC Assisted in Hurricane Maria Network Restoration, but a Clarified Disaster Response Role and Enhanced Communication Are Needed (GAO-21-297, dated 29 April 2021 and released 1 June 2021), evaluates how the Federal Communications Commission helped restore communications networks after Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands in September 2017. GAO reviewed FCC actions, such as collecting network outage data through its Disaster Information Reporting System, deploying staff to Puerto Rico, creating a Hurricane Recovery Task Force and allocating funds for network restoration, and compared them with federal emergency support guidance, interviewing agencies and companies. It found that the Department of Homeland Security's Emergency Support Function 2 guidance did not define specific actions for the FCC, and that the task force lacked transparency because its actions and findings were not published. Coverage: Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands, 2017 to 2021, federal agency level. Format and access: a free web summary and PDF report on gao.gov, a US government work in the public domain. Caveats: an institutional and policy review, with outage figures taken from FCC sources, not new measurements; one FCC recommendation was still open in May 2026. Simulation uses: evidence for emergency response and recovery assumptions in models of telecom restoration after hurricanes, and for governance roles in resilience planning. Related records: the FCC report on the 2017 hurricane season gives the outage data, and the FCC Katrina panel gives an earlier review.
